flags.why: Tiểu thư is still commonly used for a young woman from a wealthy family, including in the example given.
The verb khởi đầu is ordinary contemporary Vietnamese and is not restricted to literary language.
The regional meaning 'to bite' belongs to North Central Vietnamese, which falls under Central rather than Northern ([reference](https://en.wiktionary.org/wiki/c%E1%BA%AFm)).
Standalone y denotes medicine as a field, while the physician meaning belongs to compound forms.
Vãi used as an exclamation is vulgar slang and needs the same warning as the intensifier.
Rẽ meaning 'to turn' is standard Vietnamese used nationwide, rather than a Northern regional word ([dictionary](https://vtudien.com/viet-viet/dictionary/nghia-cua-tu-r%E1%BA%BD)).
Cột meaning 'to tie' is mainly Southern usage, but its regional restriction is missing from the warning tags.

This sense refers to a pregnant belly, not the womb or uterus ([dictionary](https://medialib.qlgd.edu.vn/Uploads/THU_VIEN/shn/1/1124/UserFiles/Tu-Dien-Tieng-Viet-Hoang-Long-thuviensach.vn-b6c5cba7-6d08-4fa4-aae4-6b53ec52276c.pdf)).
